## Features [Permalink: Features](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#features) - [x] Search Ahmia.fi from the command line - [x] Export results to CSV - [x] Enable/Disable routing requests through Tor - [x] Return results in a clean readable format - [x] Response caching for faster repeated searches - [x] Configurable result limits and request timeout ## Installation [Permalink: Installation](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#installation) **PyAhmia** is available on PyPI and can be installed like so: ``` pip install pyahmia ``` This will install `ahmia` and `pyahmia` as commands. ## Usage [Permalink: Usage](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#usage) To start searching, you can call `ahmia` (or `pyahmia`) with the specified search query. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY ``` ### Routing Traffic Through Tor (Optional) [Permalink: Routing Traffic Through Tor (Optional)](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#routing-traffic-through-tor-optional) **PyAhmia works without Tor, but you can enable routing traffic through Tor if you want.** When this is enabled, it will use Ahmia's darknet url instead of the clearnet variant. To enable routing through Tor, you can call `ahmia` with the `-t, --use-tor` flag. This assumes the tor service is running in the background, otherwise, the command will fail before you can say "hidden wiki". If Tor is not installed, you can check out the installation scripts located in [pyahmia/scripts](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia/tree/master/scripts). _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --use-tor ``` ### Exporting Output [Permalink: Exporting Output](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#exporting-output) PyAhmia only supports exporting data to csv files (for now), and in order to export, you'll need to specify the `-e, --export` flag. This will export your search results to a file named after your search query. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --export ``` ### Filtering Results by Time Period [Permalink: Filtering Results by Time Period](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#filtering-results-by-time-period) Results can be filtered by 3 time periods (day, week, month). By default, results will be taken from all time periods ( all). You can change this by using the `-p, --period` option, and pass the time period you want to get results from. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --period week ``` ### Limiting Results [Permalink: Limiting Results](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#limiting-results) By default, PyAhmia displays up to 100 results. You can change this with the `-l, --limit` option. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --limit 50 ``` To show all results regardless of the limit, use the `-a, --all` flag. _example_: ``` ahmia QUERY --all ``` ### Caching [Permalink: Caching](https://github.com/rly0nheart/pyahmia#caching) PyAhmia caches responses by default to reduce redundant requests. Configuration `example.env` contains some default values that should work out of the box. Copy this to `.env` to create your own instance of environment settings: ``` cp example.env .env ``` Review the `.env` file to ensure that it fits your needs. Here is suggestion for a more secure configuration #### /etc/security/limits.conf ``` elasticsearch - nofile unlimited elasticsearch soft memlock unlimited elasticsearch hard memlock unlimited ``` #### /etc/default/elasticsearch ``` MAX\_OPEN\_FILES=unlimited MAX\_LOCKED\_MEMORY=unlimited ``` #### /etc/elasticsearch/elasticsearch.yml ``` bootstrap.memory\_lock: true ``` #### /etc/elasticsearch/jvm.options ``` -Xms15g -Xmx15g ```` ## Tor Hidden Service Search [Permalink: Ahmia - Tor Hidden Service Search](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#ahmia---tor-hidden-service-search) ![https://ahmia.fi/](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/juhanurmi/ahmia/master/ahmia/static/images/ahmia_logo.png) [https://ahmia.fi/](https://ahmia.fi/) ## New repository! [Permalink: New repository!](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#new-repository) [https://github.com/ahmia/search](https://github.com/ahmia/search) ## Compatibility [Permalink: Compatibility](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#compatibility) Ahmia requires Python 2.7+ and Django 1.6+ The crawler is called Onionbot and it requires Apache Solr for the data. ## Installation [Permalink: Installation](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#installation) - Currently, ahmia is listening Solr from [http://127.0.0.1:33433/](http://127.0.0.1:33433/) - HTTP server is required - Please see /apache2/ to setup to run with Apache HTTP server - Note the crontabs. The order of the task is important - See crontabs file. It is strongly recommended to put crontask to another server than the web-server itself ##### Install depencies: [Permalink: Install depencies:](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#install-depencies) ``` $ apt-get install libxml2-dev libxslt-dev python-dev $ apt-get install libpq-dev $ apt-get install python-socksipy python-psycopg2 libapache2-mod-wsgi $ apt-get install libffi-dev ``` ``` $ pip install -r requirements.txt ``` ##### Furthermore, you will need to set the rights to the tools: [Permalink: Furthermore, you will need to set the rights to the tools:](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#furthermore-you-will-need-to-set-the-rights-to-the-tools) ``` $ chmod -R ugo+rx /usr/local/lib/ahmia/tools/ ``` ##### And to Apache: [Permalink: And to Apache:](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#and-to-apache) ``` $ chown -R www-data:www-data /usr/local/lib/ahmia/ $ chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o=rX /usr/local/lib/ahmia/ ``` ##### Move the Apache settings and adjust WSGI processes=X threads=Y [Permalink: Move the Apache settings and adjust WSGI processes=X threads=Y](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#move-the-apache-settings-and-adjust-wsgi-processesx-threadsy) Upper limit to memory that Apache needs is X _Y_ 8MB. For instance, 4 _16_ 8MB = 513MB. ``` cp apache2/sites-available/django-ahmia /etc/apache2/sites-available/django-ahmia /etc/init.d/apache2 restart ``` ##### And after creating the SQLite database: [Permalink: And after creating the SQLite database:](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#and-after-creating-the-sqlite-database) ``` $ chown www-data:www-data /usr/local/lib/ahmia $ chown www-data:www-data /usr/local/lib/ahmia/ahmia_db ``` ##### Not required, but recommended for better system performance: [Permalink: Not required, but recommended for better system performance:](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#not-required-but-recommended-for-better-system-performance) - Install haveged - A simple entropy daemon - Edit the process and threads parameters of the WSGIDaemonProcess in apache2/sites-available/django-ahmia - Use PostgreSQL - Install PgBouncer: a lightweight connection pooler for PostgreSQL ## Features [Permalink: Features](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#features) - Search engine for Tor hidden services. - Privacy: ahmia saves no IP logs. - Filtering child abuse. - Popularity tracking from Tor2web nodes, public WWW backlinks and the number of clicks in the search results. - Hidden service online tracker. ## Demo [Permalink: Demo](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#demo) You can try the demo by cloning this repository and running the test server with provided data: ``` $ python manage.py syncdb $ python manage.py loaddata ahmia/fixtures/initial_data.json $ python manage.py runserver ``` Then open your browser to [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000/) ## Tests [Permalink: Tests](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#tests) Unittests: ``` $ python manage.py test ahmia/tests/ ``` ## For developers [Permalink: For developers](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#for-developers) Please, at least, validate your Python code with: ``` $ pylint --rcfile=pylint.rc ./ahmia/python_code_file.py ``` and fix the major problems. ## About Ahmia hidden service search engine ### Resources [Readme](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#readme-ov-file) ### License [BSD-3-Clause license](https://github.com/juhanurmi/ahmia#BSD-3-Clause-1-ov-file) ### Uh oh!
